items.title: Phil Mead interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006
items.q: Dean Martin is mentioned by the interviewer as an example of a mid-fifties hit artist; the interviewee does not respond with any personal connection or interaction.

ctx.x: seeing where I live or if there’s something to that. But I would say that I don’t think there’s a big difference between today and the old days. I think there are a lot of really good musicians around and I think ultimately live music is what’s exciting and what makes it work. So I’m looking for a resurgence if you will, when all these young cats get out of school and get to play, and maybe we’ll see more of that. But I certainly agree with you. It seemed like in the seventies and eighties it was more we listened…

Right. Well my daughter actually did a little research for me and she came up with some of the top ten hits of around the mid-fifties. And they have such songs as “Oh My Papa” by Eddie Fisher and “Don’t Let the Stars Get in Your Eyes,” Perry Como, “That’s Amore,” Dean Martin. And then even into the rock & roll era with Bill Haley and the Comets. Now nowhere on this list are any Dixieland hits. So tell me why you came to Hamilton and were able to find people like yourself who were still into that music.
Well let me go back a little bit —
